title: Amalickiah incites the Lamanites
summary: After obtaining the kingdom, Amalickiah appoints speakers to address the Lamanites against the Nephites and seeks rule over all the land and its people.

explicit_facts.text: After obtaining the kingdom, Amalickiah appointed men to speak against the Nephites to the Lamanites from their towers.
Amalickiah sought to reign over all the land and all its people, Nephites and Lamanites alike.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Amalickiah directs the appointed speakers as they address listeners from towers.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance and design of the towers, clothing, and surroundings are not specified.

narration.text: he did appoint men to speak unto the Lamanites from their towers

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Amalickiah has become king over the Lamanites.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the speakers' words or show a battle here.

title: A host gathers for war
summary: Amalickiah gathers a numerous host to battle the Nephites, intending to overpower them and bring them into bondage.

explicit_facts.text: Amalickiah stirred the Lamanites to anger and gathered a numerous host to battle the Nephites.
He intended to overpower the Nephites and bring them into bondage.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A gathered army can be shown assembled, without depicting combat.
unspecified_visual_details: The army's size beyond 'numerous,' its equipment, and its precise gathering place are not specified.

narration.text: he had gathered together a numerous host to go to battle against the Nephites

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict battle or bondage as already occurring.

title: Zoramite chief captains
summary: Amalickiah appoints Zoramites as chief captains because they know the Nephites' strength, gathering places, and weakest city defenses.

explicit_facts.text: Amalickiah appointed chief captains from among the Zoramites, who knew the Nephites' strength, places of resort, and weakest city defenses.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Amalickiah and the appointed captains may be shown together at the appointment.
unspecified_visual_details: The place, ceremony, garments, and individual identities of the captains are not specified.

narration.text: he did appoint chief captains of the Zoramites

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent names or backstories for the captains.

title: The army moves toward Zarahemla
summary: The Lamanite army takes its camp and moves through the wilderness toward the land of Zarahemla.

explicit_facts.text: The army took its camp and moved toward the land of Zarahemla in the wilderness.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The army can be shown moving with its camp through wilderness terrain.
unspecified_visual_details: The route, landscape features, and camp equipment are not specified.

narration.text: they took their camp, and moved forth toward the land of Zarahemla in the wilderness

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict arrival or an attack.

title: Moroni prepares the people
summary: While Amalickiah obtains power by fraud and deceit, Moroni prepares the Nephites to be faithful and strengthens their armies and defenses.

explicit_facts.text: While Amalickiah obtained power by fraud and deceit, Moroni prepared the people to be faithful unto the Lord their God.
Moroni strengthened the Nephite armies and built forts, earth banks, and stone walls around cities and borders.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni can be shown overseeing defensive construction and army preparations.
unspecified_visual_details: The specific city, fort designs, materials beyond earth and stone, and Moroni's appearance are not specified.

narration.text: Moroni, on the other hand, had been preparing the minds of the people to be faithful unto the Lord their God

prohibited_inventions: Do not show Amalickiah physically present alongside Moroni; their activities are contrasted, not located together.

title: Defenses at vulnerable points
summary: Moroni places more men at the weakest fortifications, strengthening Nephite lands in preparation to protect liberty, families, peace, and worship.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni placed the greater number of men at the weakest fortifications and strengthened Nephite lands.
He prepared to support liberty, lands, wives, children, peace, and the people's ability to live unto God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephite defenders can be shown stationed at fortifications.
unspecified_visual_details: The defenders' identities, exact numbers, and the fortification's appearance are not specified.

narration.text: in their weakest fortifications he did place the greater number of men

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The defense is framed as protecting the people's liberty, families, and religious life.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an attack or portray families as present at a fort unless separately supported.

title: Moroni's character
summary: The account describes Moroni as strong and understanding, opposed to bloodshed, grateful to God, and devoted to the liberty, welfare, and safety of his people.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni was strong and mighty, had perfect understanding, did not delight in bloodshed, and rejoiced in the liberty and freedom of his country and brethren.
Moroni felt thanksgiving to God for blessings bestowed on his people and labored exceedingly for their welfare and safety.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni may be depicted alone without suggesting a specific unreported event.
unspecified_visual_details: His appearance, surroundings, and specific work are not described.

narration.text: yea, a man that did not delight in bloodshed;
a man who did labor exceedingly for the welfare and safety of his people.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses describe Moroni's character rather than narrating a specific incident or speech.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a prayer, conversation, specific labor activity, or visible divine appearance.

title: Moroni's oath
summary: Moroni is described as firm in faith in Christ and sworn to defend his people, rights, country, and religion, even at the cost of his life.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni was firm in faith in Christ and had sworn to defend his people, rights, country, and religion, even to the loss of his blood.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni may be shown standing resolutely; no oath-taking ceremony is specified.
unspecified_visual_details: The time, place, and form of the oath are not specified.

narration.text: he had sworn with an oath to defend his people, his rights, and his country, and his religion

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse reports his oath but does not narrate the moment when he made it.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific oath ceremony or injury.

title: Nephite teachings on defense
summary: The Nephites are taught to defend themselves when necessary, never to give offense, and to raise the sword only against an enemy or to preserve life; they believe God will prosper the commandment-keeping and warn them according to danger.

explicit_facts.text: The Nephites were taught to defend themselves when necessary, never to give offense, and not to raise the sword except against an enemy or to preserve their lives.
They believed God would prosper them if they kept his commandments, warn them to flee, or tell them to prepare for war according to danger.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The teaching can be conveyed as off-screen narration over a supported setting, without inventing a particular teaching audience.
unspecified_visual_details: Who taught these principles, where they were taught, and any visible audience are not specified.

narration.text: never to raise the sword except it were against an enemy

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses state the Nephites' teachings and faith, not a particular present-tense lesson.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a battle or invent a named speaker.

title: Moroni's faith
summary: Moroni believes the Lord will direct and deliver the faithful who defend themselves; he rejoices in doing good and preserving his people. The account says that people like Moroni would leave the powers of hell shaken and the devil without power over human hearts.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni believed God would make known where the people should go to defend themselves and that the Lord would deliver them.
Moroni gloried not in bloodshed but in doing good, preserving his people, keeping God's commandments, and resisting iniquity.
The narrator says that if all people were like Moroni, the powers of hell would be shaken and the devil would never have power over human hearts.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni can be shown in a reflective pose; the figure of speech about the powers of hell need not be depicted literally.
unspecified_visual_details: The specific setting and Moroni's activity are not stated.

narration.text: not in the shedding of blood but in doing good

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The powers of hell and the devil's power over hearts are expressed as a teaching, not a visible supernatural event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict hell, the devil, or supernatural forces as present.

title: Comparison with men of God
summary: The narrator compares Moroni to Ammon, the other sons of Mosiah, Alma, and Alma's sons, calling them men of God.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni is compared to Ammon, the other sons of Mosiah, Alma, and Alma's sons, who are described as men of God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni alone may be shown while the narrator's comparison is read.
unspecified_visual_details: The verse does not place the other named people physically with Moroni or specify a setting.

narration.text: for they were all men of God

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The named comparisons are narrated references, not evidence that those people are present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Ammon, Alma, or their sons as physically present in the scene.

title: Helaman and his brethren preach
summary: Helaman and his brethren preach God's word and baptize those who heed them. The people humble themselves, receive the Lord's favor, and are free from internal wars and contentions for four years.

explicit_facts.text: Helaman and his brethren preached the word of God and baptized those who hearkened to their words unto repentance.
The people humbled themselves because of their words, were highly favored of the Lord, and were free from wars and contentions among themselves for four years.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A preaching or baptismal moment is supported by verse 19; the four-year peace is a separately reported outcome, not a simultaneous event.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise preaching and baptism locations, other participants' identities, and baptismal method are not specified.

narration.text: they did preach the word of God

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The four years of peace are reported as a period, not a single visible instant.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show warfare and baptism occurring together or specify words preached.

title: Reluctantly compelled to contend
summary: In the latter end of the nineteenth year, despite peace among themselves, a group was compelled reluctantly to contend with their brethren, the Lamanites. Their wars with the Lamanites did not cease for many years.

explicit_facts.text: In the latter end of the nineteenth year, they had peace among themselves but were compelled reluctantly to contend with their brethren, the Lamanites.
Their wars with the Lamanites did not cease for many years, despite their reluctance.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The initial contention may be depicted without specifying a battle or combat actions.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, participants' numbers, and details of the contention are not specified.

narration.text: they were compelled reluctantly to contend with their brethren, the Lamanites.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The wars continuing for many years are not a single event occurring at the initial contention.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the unnamed group by a name absent from these verses.
Do not depict specific battles, casualties, or leaders not identified as present.

title: Why the Nephites take up arms
summary: The Nephites grieve taking up arms and the spiritual peril of those they send into eternity, yet cannot allow their wives and children to be massacred or their brethren to rejoice over Nephite blood while commandment-keepers remain.

explicit_facts.text: The Nephites were sorry to take up arms because they did not delight in bloodshed and grieved that many brethren would die unprepared to meet God.
They could not lay down their lives and allow their wives and children to be massacred by those who had joined the Lamanites to destroy them.
They could not bear their brethren rejoicing over Nephite blood while people who kept God's commandments remained.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A restrained image of Nephites contemplating their defensive duty can accompany the narrator's account.
unspecified_visual_details: No specific decision-making gathering, weapons, family members, attack, or battle is narrated.

narration.text: they did not delight in the shedding of blood

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The threatened massacre and rejoicing over blood are described as reasons for resistance, not events happening in this moment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a massacre, bloodshed, combat, or the brethren rejoicing as a present event.
